title: Eight-face conjecture for facets of the Newton polytope
statement:
Let $\mathbf{N}_{3,n}$ be the Newton polytope, and let $\gamma_{j_1,j_2,j_3}$ be the generalized positive root

$$
\gamma_{j_1,j_2,j_3}=\sum_{t=j_1}^{j_2-2}\alpha_{1,t}+\sum_{t=j_2-1}^{j_3-3}\alpha_{2,t}.
$$

Assume that $\{j_1,j_2,j_3\}$ is totally nonfrozen, meaning that no two indices are cyclically adjacent. The generalized positive roots are linear functions on $\mathbb{R}^{2\times(n-3)}$.

**Eight-face conjecture.** The facet of $\mathbf{N}_{3,n}$ minimizing $\gamma_{j_1,j_2,j_3}$ has exactly eight codimension-$3$ faces combinatorially isomorphic to

$$
\mathbf{N}_{3,j_2-j_1+2}\times\mathbf{N}_{3,j_3-j_2+2}\times\mathbf{N}_{3,j_1-j_3+n+2}.
$$

These faces correspond to the eight weakly separated collections listed in the source. The claim generalizes the observed three-split structure and remains unproved in the supplied text.
source_name: Nick Early, “Factorization for Generalized Biadjoint Scalar Amplitudes via Matroid Subdivisions”, arXiv:2211.16623 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.16623

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).
